note: The ten floors built from the evacuation-plan sheets by tools/evacpipe -- the input for the future routing layer. This is NOT data/floors.json, which describes the legacy CAD build (data/L<n>/) that the shipped app reads.
coordinates: Each floor is in its own sheet's pixel frame (origin top-left, x right, y down, canvas imageWidth x imageHeight). The sheets are not at one scale, nor at one scale in x and y: each floor's `metres.pxPerMetre` gives pixels per metre along its own axes (sourced from the CAD by tools/evacpipe/metres.py; read its docstring before trusting a figure). Lakeside floors also carry `metres.toCampus`, an affine [a, b, c, d, e, f] taking sheet (x, y) to campus metres (a*x + b*y + c, d*x + e*y + f) in the CAD's frame, so the six stack; Toh Tuck's four carry one too, fitted on stair cores, lifts, the bridge door and corners (turned about 25 degrees), and TT_L1 a `clip` polygon (sheet px) outside which the map does not draw it. `ffl` is the finished floor level in metres. Floors connect only through connector portals.
connectorConvention: A stair or lift keeps the same portal id on every floor it serves (STAIR-<n> type "stair", ELEV-<n> type "elevator"); its link lists the other floors in vertical order. See tools/evacpipe/connectors.py. A linkway bridge between Lakeside L<n> and Toh Tuck TT_L<n> is BRIDGE-<n> type "bridge" (n = 2, 3, 4), marked sameLevelAs on both ends: a ramp, never a flight.

lakeside-west.what: Lakeside's west side (library, theatre, music block, atrium, Stairs 1-4, the lift ELEV-1) is drawn about 10 m too far north on every sheet, relative to the pods, which are within a few metres of the CAD. Inside `region` (campus metres, hard edges), campus y moves by `dy` (piecewise linear in y, metres): north-south only, so rooms stay rectangles. The east edge runs on the wall line between the west side's rooms and the pods' (no room straddles it).

anchors._: true campus metres from the CAD (stair cores = clusters of the stair layer, the lift box, the atrium balustrade circle; per sheet through floor_transforms.json and the dimension-chain scale), and where the sheets put them (app, L3)
